slot.brief: Rank a set of elements by ionisation enthalpy or electron gain enthalpy (e.g., noble gases vs halogens vs group 2) and pick correct order

stem: Which sequence gives the elements in increasing order of their first electron gain enthalpy?

verdicts.working: First electron gain enthalpies are approximately Cl: −349, S: −200, Ca: −2, Ne: positive (kJ mol⁻¹). Thus the increasing order is Cl < S < Ca < Ne.

working:
$\Delta H_{eg}(\text{Cl})\approx-349 < \Delta H_{eg}(\text{S})\approx-200 < \Delta H_{eg}(\text{Ca})\approx-2 < \Delta H_{eg}(\text{Ne})>0$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.

Independent check: First electron gain enthalpies are approximately Cl: −349, S: −200, Ca: −2, Ne: positive (kJ mol⁻¹). Thus the increasing order is Cl < S < Ca < Ne.
solution:
First electron gain enthalpy becomes more negative as electron addition becomes more favorable. The approximate values are
$$\Delta H_{eg}(\text{Cl})\approx-349 < \Delta H_{eg}(\text{S})\approx-200 < \Delta H_{eg}(\text{Ca})\approx-2 < \Delta H_{eg}(\text{Ne})>0\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}.$$
Hence, the increasing order is $\text{Cl}<\text{S}<\text{Ca}<\text{Ne}$.
